problem_sources.text: ﻿Problem Statements of Nakshatra, The AEROSPACE HACKATHON 2026 HARDWARE TRACK PROBLEM STATEMENT 01: Autonomous Lunar Rover for Surface Exploration and Hazard Avoidance Lunar exploration missions require robotic systems capable of navigating challenging and uncertain terrain with limited human intervention. Build a small-scale rover prototype capable of autonomous or semi-autonomous navigation over an uneven, obstacle-laden test terrain (provided at the venue as a sandbox/course simulating craters, slopes, and debris). The rover must use onboard sensing (e.g., camera, ultrasonic, IR, or LiDAR) to detect obstacles, steep slopes, or unstable regions in real time and adjust its path accordingly. Deliverables: working rover + live/recorded demo run on the test terrain; brief writeup of the perception and navigation approach. Evaluation criteria: successful hazard detection rate, navigation efficiency (path taken vs. optimal), and autonomy level (manual intervention count). PROBLEM STATEMENT 02: Satellite Component Health Monitoring and Fault Detection System Satellite subsystems operate continuously under harsh environmental and operational conditions, where undetected component degradation or failure can affect overall mission performance. Build a modular, hardware-based satellite health-monitoring system using a CubeSat-like cube structure containing multiple interchangeable sensor packs. Each sensor pack should monitor one or more representative satellite components or subsystems. The sensor packs may include temperature, vibration, voltage, current, battery/power, or other relevant sensors. The packs should be physically distributed across the cube so that the system can demonstrate multi-point monitoring rather than sensing only a single component. A central controller shall acquire the sensor data, identify abnormal behaviour or injected faults, and present the health status locally through indicators or a dashboard. Deliverables: working CubeSat-like prototype with multiple sensor packs; live demonstration of continuous health monitoring; at least one injected fault or abnormal condition detected and flagged; brief documentation of the sensor-pack architecture and fault-detection logic. Evaluation criteria: fault-detection accuracy, number and usefulness of monitored parameters, multi-point sensing capability, response latency, modularity of the sensor packs, and clarity of health-status reporting. PROBLEM STATEMENT 03: Radiation and Space-Weather Monitor Spacecraft electronics are exposed to radiation and changing space-weather conditions that can disturb sensors, communication systems, memory, power electronics, and other onboard devices. Build a compact hardware sensor payload that monitors radiation-related conditions and relevant environmental or electrical parameters, and provides an indication of abnormal or potentially hazardous conditions for spacecraft electronics. The prototype may combine a radiation sensor or radiation-detection module with supporting sensors such as temperature, voltage, current, magnetic-field, or other space-weather indicators. The system should continuously record the measurements and identify abnormal levels, trends, or sudden changes. Where direct space radiation cannot be safely reproduced, teams may use a controlled laboratory stimulus or a validated simulation/emulation method to demonstrate the response of the monitoring system. Deliverables: working compact sensor payload; live or recorded demonstration of radiation/space-weather parameter monitoring; abnormal-condition detection and alert; data logging or dashboard; brief documentation of the sensing, calibration, detection, and alert mechanism. Evaluation criteria: measurement reliability, detection of abnormal conditions, response latency, quality of data logging and visualization, robustness of the hardware, and relevance of the demonstrated monitoring approach to spacecraft electronics. SOFTWARE TRACK PROBLEM STATEMENT 01: Rapid Flood Extent Mapping and Settlement Impact Assessment for the Nepal Terai Nepal's Terai belt floods almost every monsoon, cutting off highways and villages along the Koshi, Bagmati, and Gandaki basins, and disaster authorities need a same-day flooded-area map to act on. Build an automated pipeline that compares pre-flood and post-flood optical satellite imagery of a Terai river sector, detects newly flooded regions using spectral water indices, and identifies which towns /cities are affected. Suggested datasets: Sentinel-2 L2A or Landsat-8/9 surface reflectance data Deliverables: pipeline/code; flood extent map (raster or vector) with an affected-settlement report on at least one test scene. Evaluation criteria: flood detection accuracy against a reference cloud-free/ground-truth mask where available, correctness of settlement impact flags, and clarity of the visualization. PROBLEM STATEMENT 02: Lunar Permanently Shadowed Region Mapping and Surface Hazard Assessment Permanently shadowed regions (PSRs) near the lunar poles present challenging environments for future exploration due to extreme illumination conditions and uncertain, hazardous terrain. Build a geospatial pipeline that identifies PSRs and generates a classified surface hazard map using terrain indicators such as slope, roughness, and shadow extent. Suggested datasets: Chandrayaan-2 OHRC/TMC-2, LRO LOLA/Diviner, or equivalent public lunar elevation/optical datasets Deliverables: PSR identification output + a classified hazard raster/map with at least 3 hazard categories (e.g., safe / caution / unsafe). Evaluation criteria: correctness of PSR delineation, hazard classification consistency, and map interpretability. NAKSHATRA is an aerospace-focused hackathon organised by the Aerospace Club, Madhav Institute of Technology & Science (MITS), Gwalior, bringing together students to innovate and solve real-world challenges across space, astronomy, aeronautics, and aerospace technology.

The hackathon provides participants with the opportunity to develop innovative and practical solutions through two dedicated tracks, Software and Hardware, featuring aerospace-specific problem statements.

Competition Format

Round 1: Ideation & PPT Submission Round

The first round will evaluate teams based on their understanding of the selected aerospace problem statement, the proposed approach, innovation, feasibility, and potential impact.

Teams must select ONE problem statement from either the Software or Hardware track and submit a detailed solution PPT following the prescribed format.

Submission Requirements:

  • Teams can choose one problem statement from either the Software or Hardware track.

  • The submitted PPT must clearly present the selected problem statement and proposed solution.

  • The solution should cover the proposed approach, key benefits, innovation, technology stack, and high-level system architecture, along with other details specified in the PPT format.

  • Teams must complete the Google Form and submit their solution PPT within the specified deadline.

  • The detailed PPT format and submission instructions are provided to participants.

Form Link: Click Here

Problem Statement Details: Click Here

PPT Format: Click Here

Teams that fail to complete the Google Form will not be considered for further evaluation.

Shortlisted teams will qualify for the Final Round.

Round 2: Final Hackathon

The top 50 shortlisted teams from Round 1 will participate in the 12-hour offline Final Hackathon.

Mode: Offline
Duration: 12 Hours
Date: 24-25 October 2026
Venue: MITS Campus, Gwalior

The Final Round will provide shortlisted teams with an opportunity to build, test, refine, and demonstrate their proposed solutions. Teams will be evaluated on the functionality, technical implementation, innovation, feasibility, and demonstration of their solution.

Participation Guidelines

  • Open to college/university students.

  • Team Size: 2-4 members.

  • Inter-college teams are allowed.

  • Inter-branch/inter-specialisation teams are allowed.

  • Each team can participate in either the Software or Hardware track.

  • Each team can select one problem statement only.

  • Each track features aerospace-specific problem statements.

  • The problem statement selected during Round 1 will be carried forward to the Final Round.

  • Only shortlisted teams will advance to the offline Final Hackathon.

  • Further instructions, venue guidelines, and requirements for the Final Round will be communicated to shortlisted teams.

Rules

  • Each participant can be a member of only one team.

  • Each team must consist of 2–4 members.

  • Teams must select and work on one problem statement only.

  • The submitted solution must be the original work of the participating team.

  • Plagiarism, copying, impersonation, or misrepresentation may result in disqualification.

  • Teams must complete the required registration/submission form and submit their PPT within the specified deadline.

  • Shortlisted teams must participate in the offline Final Hackathon at MITS, Gwalior.

  • Participants must follow all instructions, safety guidelines, and requirements issued by the organising team.

  • The decision of the judging panel will be final.

  • The organisers reserve the right to modify the schedule, rules, or other event details if required. Any such changes will be communicated to participants.

Teams selected for the Final Round will receive further information regarding the venue, reporting time, required materials, evaluation process, and other Final Round guidelines.
